text: atmosphere ocean coupled exchanges heat, moisture, momentum air-sea interface. Sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies influence atmospheric convection circulation, wind stress anomalies drive ocean currents upwelling. bidirectional coupling gives rise internal modes climate variability can persist months decades [2]. strength ocean-atmosphere coupling varies geographically. tropical Pacific, strong coupling arises shallow thermocline Walker circulation feedback, enabling ENSO. tropical Atlantic exhibits moderate coupling multiple SST modes including AMO, TNA, TSA, Atlantic Nino. Extratropical oceans show weaker coupling ocean integrates atmospheric forcing rather driving . polar regions, ice-albedo feedback amplifies climate variability. climate oscillation indices capture either SST patterns direct measures ocean thermal state (Nino indices, AMO, PDO); pressure patterns measures atmospheric circulation (NAO, AO, SOI, PNA); combined metrics multivariate indices capturing components (MEI, BEST).

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: ENSO dominant mode interannual climate variability, global teleconnections affecting weather patterns, ecosystems, human societies worldwide [3]. phenomenon involves coupled fluctuations tropical Pacific SST atmospheric pressure.

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: canonical ENSO cycle involves positive feedback SST, trade winds, thermocline depth: El Nino phase, weakening easterly trade winds reduces equatorial upwelling, allowing warm water accumulate central-eastern Pacific. Atmospheric convection shifts eastward, reduced pressure gradient weakens trades Bjerknes feedback mechanism. La Nina phase, enhanced easterly trade winds intensify equatorial upwelling, bringing cold water surface eastern Pacific. Convection intensifies western Pacific warm pool, increased pressure gradient reinforces strong trades. oscillation period irregular, typically 2-7 years, events lasting 9-12 months.

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: ENSO influences global climate atmospheric teleconnections [10]. El Nino events bring warm dry conditions Australia, Indonesia, Southeast Asia; drought southern Africa; flooding Peru Ecuador; warm winters Canada northern US; increased Atlantic hurricane wind shear resulting fewer hurricanes; enhanced California rainfall. La Nina events produce enhanced monsoons Australia Southeast Asia; drought US Southwest South America; cold winters northern US; reduced Atlantic hurricane wind shear leading hurricanes.

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: PDO represents leading pattern North Pacific SST variability north 20N [11]. Unlike ENSO, PDO exhibits persistence decadal timescales “regime shifts” occurring roughly every 20-30 years. PDO calculated leading EOF monthly SST anomalies North Pacific removing global mean SST trend. pattern shows warm (cool) anomalies eastern Pacific; cool (warm) anomalies central North Pacific forming horseshoe pattern; strongest signal Kuroshio-Oyashio extension.  PDO exhibited distinct regime shifts instrumental record: positive phase 1925 1946; negative phase 1947 1976; positive phase 1977 1998; negative phase 1999 2013; mixed conditions 2014 present.
code: plot_index(   climate_monthly,   "PDO",   fill_anomaly = TRUE,   smooth = 0.05,   title = "Pacific decadal oscillation" )

text: IPO basin-scale counterpart PDO, capturing coherent SST variability across entire Pacific [12]. title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: NAO dominant pattern atmospheric variability North Atlantic, governing weather climate eastern North America western Europe [21]. NAO defined pressure difference Icelandic Low Azores High. Two versions commonly used: CPC NAO, based rotated EOF analysis 500 hPa heights; Jones NAO, station-based index using Gibraltar Iceland observations available since 1821.  NAO influences European winter climate, positive phases bringing mild wet conditions northern Europe; US East Coast winter storms; Greenland ice sheet mass balance; North Atlantic ecosystems fisheries.
code: plot_indices(   climate_monthly,   indices = c("NAO", "NAO_Jones"),   start_year = 1900,   title = "NAO indices comparison" )

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: PNA pattern second leading mode Northern Hemisphere winter variability AO [22]. consists four centers action: North Pacific opposite sign tropics; western Canada sign tropics; Gulf Alaska sign tropics; southeastern US opposite sign. Positive PNA phases feature enhanced ridge western North America; warm, dry conditions US Northwest; cold, wet conditions Southeast US; enhanced Aleutian Low.  PNA responds ENSO forcing: El Nino tends produce positive PNA, La Nina produces negative PNA.
code: plot_index(   climate_monthly,   "PNA",   fill_anomaly = TRUE,   title = "Pacific North American pattern" )

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: NP index area-weighted sea level pressure 30-65N, 160E-140W [24]. Low NP indicates deeper Aleutian Low, associated enhanced Pacific storm track, warm SST along North American coast, ecosystem regime shifts affecting Pacific salmon zooplankton.

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: Indian Ocean Dipole coupled ocean-atmosphere mode tropical Indian Ocean [26]. involves anomalous SST gradients western (Arabian Sea) eastern (Indonesia) Indian Ocean. Dipole Mode Index (DMI) calculated : \[\text{DMI} = \text{SSTA}_{\text{west}} - \text{SSTA}_{\text{east}}\] : - West: 50-70E, 10S-10N - East: 90-110E, 10S-0

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: Positive IOD events feature cool SST near Indonesia due anomalous upwelling, warm SST western Indian Ocean, drought Indonesia Australia, enhanced rainfall East Africa, effects can amplify counteract ENSO. Negative IOD events feature warm SST near Indonesia, cool western Indian Ocean temperatures, -normal Australian rainfall.

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: IOD can occur independently ENSO often develops conjunction El Nino events [27]. El Nino positive IOD co-occur, impacts Australia amplified (severe drought).

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: QBO dominant mode variability equatorial stratosphere, characterized alternating easterly westerly wind regimes descend stratosphere period approximately 28 months [28]. QBO index represents zonal wind specific pressure level (typically 30 50 hPa) equator.  QBO generated upward-propagating tropical waves, easterly westerly phases descending approximately 1 km per month, phase lasting 12-16 months. QBO modulates polar vortex strength; influences Atlantic hurricane activity, westerly phases associated hurricanes; affects tropical convection monsoons; interacts solar cycle.
code: plot_index(   climate_monthly,   "QBO",   fill_anomaly = TRUE,   title = "Quasi-Biennial Oscillation (30 hPa)" )

title: Climate oscillations: theory, indices and drivers
text: Indian monsoon index measures June-September rainfall core monsoon region India [29]. monsoon delivers ~80% India’s annual rainfall, critical agriculture. title: User guide: accessing and visualizing climate indices
text: oscillatoRs package provides access 43 planetary climate oscillation indices authoritative sources including NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory (PSL) Climate Prediction Center (CPC). package includes pre-bundled datasets covering major climate modes; functions download updated data directly source; publication-quality visualization tools; utilities cross-index correlation analysis.

title: oscillatoRs: Planetary climate oscillation indices and teleconnections from NOAA PSL and CPC — oscillatoRs-package
text: Download, process, visualize 43 planetary climate oscillation indices authoritative sources including NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory (PSL) Climate Prediction Center (CPC). package includes pre-bundled datasets covering major climate modes: ENSO (SOI, Nino regions, ONI, MEI), Pacific multidecadal variability (PDO, IPO), Atlantic oscillations (AMO, TNA, TSA), polar oscillations (AO, AAO, NAO), Indian Ocean Dipole (DMI), stratospheric dynamics (QBO), atmospheric teleconnections (PNA, WP, EP/NP). Provides functions downloading updated data, creating publication-quality time series visualizations, computing cross-index correlations.
